solutions.check: 31 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Work time? Almost put away handle

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so one letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time
to put food away is to eat it, ATE, here losing its A

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is time to work, having nearly tidied away the tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' is slang for eating a meal, and 'almost' drops one of its letters; Cyclops lets the A go rather than the usual final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to work its controls, the same as handling it.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Cutting Bill's inverted whatsit

indicators.note: something inverted is turned the other way round, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: AC is an account or bill, with the 's attached
a whatsit is a thing whose name escapes you

explanation.surface: Someone is trimming a gadget belonging to a man called Bill, which is upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name, but it is AC, the abbreviation for account; the possessive 's comes along and the pair turns round to SCA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is a harsh, wounding one, exactly what a scathing comment is.

clue.text: He would say "Back, swine!", being a prickly character

parts.note: to hedge a bet is to back the other side as insurance
a hog is a pig

explanation.surface: A grumpy, touchy man shouts at someone to get back, calling them a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal itself would 'say' its own name as an order: back (HEDGE) plus swine (HOG). 'Back' is a verb meaning to support, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is covered in spines, so it is literally prickly; a character can also mean a creature.

clue.text: Is Trump beginning to be trapped in current upset?

indicators.note: whatever is trapped sits inside something else, enclosed by it

parts.note: a draught is a current of air
taken as written

indicators.note: a beginning is where a word starts, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Trump

explanation.surface: A question whether Trump is starting to be caught up in the present turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present' in the surface but is a flow of air through a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distraught is extremely agitated and troubled, a strong way of being upset.

clue.text: Holding back, like our old monarch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hesitant, not prepared to act
second meaning: the epithet of an Anglo-Saxon English king

explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred the Unready was an English king around the year 1000; his nickname actually meant 'ill-advised', but it reads as unprepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not prepared or reluctant to act is hesitating, and the word is also the famous nickname of King Ethelred.

clue.text: Canon making a royal take pill, oddly left out

indicators.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left, and leaving it out removes that letter
done oddly means done strangely, so the letters fall into an unusual order

parts.note: a prince is a member of a royal family
the pill being taken, losing one of its two Ls

explanation.surface: A churchman becomes a royal by swallowing a tablet, with something strange left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like 'take every other letter', but here it is the mixing signal, and 'left out' drops one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a general rule or standard, so it is a synonym for a governing principle.

clue.text: Just one nut — exercise on toilet

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
can is American slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone does a workout sitting on the loo, with a joke about having only one testicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' invites the slang reading of a testicle, but it is a real nut; 'on' means placed above, as in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a type of edible nut from a hickory tree, so it is an example of a nut.

clue.text: 'FU' in digital terms

parts.note: surface reading: a rude two-letter insult expressed in computer or electronic language
setter's reading: digital means done with the digits, the fingers, so the insult is made by hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests technology, but digits are fingers. In Britain, two fingers raised with the palm inward is an obscene insult, much like the middle finger.
explanation.definitionFit: The rude British two-finger hand gesture conveys the same contemptuous message as the printed insult.

clue.text: By way of abandoning a right, America creates Covid-19?

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is removed

parts.note: VIA means by way of; it drops the letter a
R is the abbreviation for right
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A dig suggesting that America, by giving up a right, produced the pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' in 'abandoning a right' is the letter A, which comes out of VIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Covid-19 is the illness caused by a coronavirus, so it is offered as an example with a question mark.

clue.text: (& 2dn./17dn.) Trump: "Proper success" "Good father" (very low in star ranking)

parts.note: proper or correct
a win is a success

indicators.note: the word is reduced to its opening letter as the standard short form used in grades

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
pop is an informal word for father
a joke grade of celebrity, far down the alphabet below the A-list

explanation.surface: Trump's slogans praising himself, set against a jibe that he barely ranks as a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Celebrities are graded A-list down to Z-list; the setter coins a U-list for someone near the bottom. The answer spans 10 across, 2 down and 17 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump is a leading example of a politician on the nationalist political right who appeals to ordinary voters against elites.

clue.text: Another nail in the coffin with Conservative leader screwing up — get irate

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the word supplies just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Conservative

indicators.note: screwing something up messes it about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be scrambled

explanation.surface: A Tory leader's bungling is another fatal blow to the party, making people angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nail in the coffin' suggests political doom, but it is the old slang for each smoke shortening a life.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokes were long called coffin nails, since each one was said to bring the smoker closer to death.

clue.text: Is No. 10 written off? It's stress

indicators.note: a car that is written off is wrecked, so the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the abbreviation for number
the number spelt out

explanation.surface: Worry over whether Downing Street, the Prime Minister's office, has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 10 Downing Street is the Prime Minister's residence, but here it simply gives NO and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental or emotional strain, a direct synonym for stress.

clue.text: You'll really admire yourself having this combination of bloomers and S&M

definitions.text: You'll really admire yourself having this

parts.note: narcissi are spring flowers, plural of narcissus
the two letters as printed

explanation.surface: A boast that you'll be very pleased with yourself wearing big knickers along with bondage gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are old-fashioned baggy knickers, but here they are flowers that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-admiration is the meaning of the word, named after the youth in Greek myth who loved his reflection.

clue.text: It's hard on Private Eye gang, mate!

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the clue appears in Private Eye, so the magazine is 'us'
a band is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A complaint that life is tough on the staff of the satirical magazine, addressed to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine; since this puzzle runs in it, the magazine refers to itself as US. 'Mate' looks like a friendly address but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a spouse or partner, and a married man is his wife's partner.

clue.text: Pain-in-the-arse Democrat leads Republican with a lot of money

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
R is the abbreviation for Republican
taken as written
G is a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An irritating Democrat is ahead of a wealthy Republican in a US race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' places the Democrat first rather than meaning a poll lead; G for a grand is a common shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious or irksome is a drag, informal for a nuisance or annoyance.

clue.text: (& 19dn.)Vast whorehouse almost at end of tether, as seen on TV

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: vast means very large, so a three-letter word for large is wanted
a brothel, shorn of its last letter

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: the last letter of tether

explanation.surface: A huge brothel's staff are nearly at the end of their tether, as filmed for television.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans 16 across and 19 down. 'At the end of one's tether' is an idiom for exasperation, but here it just supplies R.
explanation.definitionFit: The reality television series locks contestants in a house under constant camera surveillance, so it is something seen on TV.

clue.text: Uncivilised Spike 'misused' cigar — not good

indicators.note: not means without, and good is abbreviated to its single letter, which is removed

parts.note: a barb is a sharp spike

indicators.note: something misused is put to the wrong use, so the letters go into the wrong order

parts.note: cigar without its G

explanation.surface: A savage named Spike abuses a cigar, which is not a nice thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike looks like a man's name, but it is a spike, a BARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbaric behaviour is savage and primitive, lacking civilisation, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Penny wants to get on courtier

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny wants to get along with a member of the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny reads as a name but is the coin abbreviation P; 'get on' means grow older, not get along.
explanation.definitionFit: A page was a boy attendant serving at a royal or noble court, so he counts as a courtier.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Balls could get kicked here, but nudist's failed to start playing with a 'scrotum base'

indicators.note: failing to start means the beginning never happens, so the first letter is lost
playing with something is fiddling about, so the letters get moved around

parts.note: nudist without its first letter; the 's is 'has'
taken as written

indicators.note: the base of a down word is its bottom, its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of scrotum

explanation.surface: A crude picture of a naked man's private parts getting kicked during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'balls' are footballs, not testicles; 'nudist's' means 'nudist has', so the 's gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports ground where football is played is an arena in which balls are kicked about.

clue.text: see 16ac.
Times head writes awful lot of wind

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Times

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: The editor of The Times produces dreadful writing that is mostly hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot of wind' suggests pompous talk, but it is a weather phenomenon.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is an American informal name for a tornado, a violent column of rotating wind.

clue.text: Message from Times taking the piss

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: T stands for time, so two make a plural
wee is a childish word for urine

explanation.surface: A note from The Times newspaper is mocking someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking the piss' is British slang for mocking, but here 'taking' is the container and 'piss' is WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short message posted on the social media platform once called Twitter.

clue.text: Jack, having an erection, tries recklessly cutting end off — God!

indicators.note: cutting off an end trims away a final letter

parts.note: J is jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: done recklessly means done wildly, so the letters scatter

parts.note: to have an erection is to be up
tries without its last letter

explanation.surface: A lewd scene: aroused Jack rashly attempts some cutting, then someone cries out to God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God!' looks like an exclamation of horror; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter was king of the gods in Roman mythology, so he is a god.

clue.text: Jack reformed our party at the heart, being one to pin the blame?

parts.note: J is jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again in a new shape, so the letters rearrange

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of party

explanation.surface: Jack has transformed the heart of our political party, and may be the one who gets blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes Jack the scapegoat; in fact the answer is the person who assigns blame by voting guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury member decides guilt in a trial, so is literally someone who fixes blame on the accused.

clue.text: Sid's turned on by boobs? It'll lead to ruin

indicators.note: turned means spun round, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the name taken as written, with 's meaning 'is'
re means on, concerning
a pair of breasts

explanation.surface: Sid is aroused by breasts, and someone warns it will be his undoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' reads as aroused, but 'turned' reverses Sid and 'on' is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in disrepair has fallen into a ruinous, neglected state, so the noun matches ruin.

clue.text: Fair, being an easy pick-up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pale in colour, as of hair or skin
second meaning: not heavy, so easy to lift

explanation.surface: A woman described as fair is also an easy pick-up, a person readily seduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick-up' suggests a casual sexual partner, but it means something lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pale-coloured, like fair hair, and also having little weight, so easy to lift.

clue.text: Act bullish, as ex-presidential hopeful?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pierce with horns, as a bull does
second meaning: Al, the US vice president who lost the 2000 election

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bullish' sounds like confident in finance, but here it means behaving like a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull wounds with its horns, and Al Gore ran for the US presidency in 2000 and lost.

clue.text: In the lead? Fix! Overturn!

parts.note: a team in the lead is up
to fix is to set

explanation.surface: A crowd cries foul about a rigged contest and demands the result be reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' suggests a rigged result, but it is simply SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn something is to knock it over, which is one sense of the verb upset.

clue.text: Having been elected, Kitty's set aside

parts.note: a party that wins an election is in
a kitty is a pooled reserve of money

explanation.surface: After winning office, someone has had their cat put to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat or a name, but it is a fund of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money kept in reserve is saved for later use, the meaning of put or set aside.
